question: Suraj travels at a speed of 30 kmph. Find the distance covered by him in 72 seconds.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert speed directly to m/s and multiply by time to find the distance.

Distance = Speed × Time

Distance = 30 × (5/18) × 72

Distance = (25/3) × 72 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Suraj = 30 kmph

Time taken = 72 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

1 kmph = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, convert the speed into m/s.

⇒ Speed = 30 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Speed = 150/18 m/s = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Now, substitute the values into the distance formula.

⇒ Distance = (25/3) × 72

⇒ Distance = 25 × 24

⇒ Distance = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply the speed by 18/5.

Average Speed

When traveling equal distances at different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed formula is (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two objects are moving in the same direction, relative speed is |S₁ − S₂|. In opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.
